sections.title: Reliable SQLite WAL recovery and bounded shutdown
items: Open supported installations using the committed SQLite main database and WAL together, including partially checkpointed databases and missing or stale SHM indexes, without manual checkpoint or data reconstruction.

Validate WAL snapshots in a private temporary copy before opening the original writer. Reject unsupported identities, versions, schema and corrupt snapshots while preserving the original installation files.

Treat busy or incomplete checkpoints and storage/log close failures as unconfirmed shutdown with a nonzero exit status. Keep installation ownership through actual database cleanup and final log closure.

Bound internal transaction draining and concurrent close waits by the remaining shutdown budget. Cancel and roll back unfinished transactions, prevent late writes from old callbacks, and preserve committed data and Work/Service intent.

sections.title: Core restart reliability
items: Use Desktop and CLI with Core installations recovered directly from committed SQLite WAL. Saved sessions, installation identity and Work/Service selections are retained through supported recovery.
Continue using the browser entry on port 17891 and the Core API on port 17871, with the existing Linux amd64 CLI and Desktop interfaces.

sections.title: Core-managed diagnostic log exports
items: Preserve safe platform logs and bounded Agent/Service archives in the installation data directory, and export retained Core logs plus the requesting administrator's own Work logs without stopping Works.
Produce an immutable ZIP with a fixed cutoff, source manifest, checksums and explicit gaps. Recover accepted tasks with their original idempotency key and download the same retained result again.
Keep administrator and task-owner authorization through collection and download, redact known credentials including short values, and preserve valid UTF-8 across streamed chunks.
Provide logs export, logs show and logs download in piwork-cli. Simplify startup help while preserving the existing runtime ports and authentication.

sections.title: Export troubleshooting logs from Desktop
items: Use the single Export logs entry in the administrator account menu to collect logs, create the archive and start a browser download through the existing UI origin.
Show real collection stages and incomplete sources, recover a lost create response with the original key, and retain the original task when detail reads temporarily fail.
Start at most one automatic download for the current intent and use Download again for the same package. Save the ZIP and send it to a trusted maintainer manually; no upload service is included.

sections.title: Simplified Linux delivery
items: Start piwork-core directly with only --ui-port, --core-port and --data-dir. The integrated workbench, administration and setup use HTTP on port 17891; Core HTTP listens on port 17871 for local and remote clients.
Retire piwork-serve, its piwork alias, standalone Console and terminal Core management commands. Preserve operator identity, protected administration APIs, user authorization and Work data.
Deliver only piwork-core and piwork-cli for Linux amd64. Keep Agent, MCP and helpers in their runtime images.
Replace local build and release outputs only after validation, with current production image identities, bilingual materials and checksums.

sections.title: Guided setup and administration
items: Keep configuration reads and saved-model recovery local to Quick setup, preserve unsaved input and focus, and show concrete dependency preparation before opening the workbench.
Recommend the direct DeepSeek API with an ordinary platform link that preserves the current setup draft.
Preserve management navigation and account menu state while background status reads complete.

sections.title: Linux native client
items: Use piwork-cli without a subcommand to open Desktop, or use its user commands to connect to an existing Core. Closing the client does not stop Core or Works.
Retire native Windows delivery and the CLI Docker image. Linux and Windows browsers can continue to use the Core web interface.
Keep user credentials, local Desktop and proxy behavior, Work commands, files, packages and snapshots.

sections.title: Clear progress and Service feedback
items: Use consistent local pending indicators without replacing focused controls, live Service frames or recovery links.
Tie Service startup, failures, diagnostics and bounded logs to the original Service while keeping unrelated Services usable.
Keep chat composer focus, narrow-screen model controls, session choices and export progress readable.

sections.title: Independent ControlPlane and Core with one-command startup
items: Start two independent HTTP services in one Linux process: ControlPlane defaults to 0.0.0.0:17891 for browsers, while Core defaults to 127.0.0.1:17871 for backend and CLI clients.
Use the workbench, administration, setup, files, event streams and prefix-aware Services through the single browser port 17891.
Keep Core authorization and lifecycle ownership behind a real HTTP boundary; explicitly set --core-listen when remote CLI access is required.
Remove the hosted Service port pool and cross-port grants; trusted Service applications share the ControlPlane origin and must support dynamic URL prefixes.
Allow configuration saves to overlap published context reads without intermittent lock failures.

sections.title: Service access through the browser entry
items: Open hosted Services at /services/<workId>/<serviceId>/<port>/, including HTTP, SSE and WebSocket, without additional browser ports or DNS configuration.
Ship prefix-aware official NiceGUI templates and runtime helpers with scoped drafts and application resource URLs.
Keep independent CLI Desktop and its local Host entry, proxy and credentials separate from the hosted ControlPlane.
Existing root-path applications and captured images require explicit adaptation; imports retain their original source, images and data.
Keep hosted Service entry probes stable across runtime restarts while revalidating the new instance and closing old streams.

sections.title: One-command Linux startup and browser setup
items: Start Core, the web workbench and administration from one Linux program or Docker container, then open the server IP in a browser.
Create the first administrator directly, with password confirmation, then sign in normally and configure a model and CoreRuntime through Quick setup.
Use matching embedded Agent and helper image defaults without manual image configuration or model environment variables.
Remove private setup links and terminal browser authorization while preserving account login, CSRF protection and Work ownership checks.

sections.title: Open, sign in and work
items: Open Desktop directly without Access pages, browser tickets or terminal approval; local Desktop restores ordinary sessions and can reuse a valid saved Core login.
Use consistent Quick setup, Admin navigation and account menu interactions, with clear preparation progress before opening the workbench.
Recover slow session initialization through Retry connection without replaying business actions.
Use the simplified bilingual project READMEs and updated one-command installation guides.

sections.title: Desktop workflows and recovery
items: Ship matching release components for the updated Desktop workspace and export workflows.
Keep existing Core APIs, storage format, authorization and managed Work runtime behavior unchanged in this preview.

sections.title: Desktop workflows and recovery
items: Continue one explicit export through the original Operation, snapshot and transfer to a verified browser download, including close/navigation and lost-response recovery.
Preserve the current Service, Chat drafts and per-file editing context through transient reads and workspace navigation; open imported Works only after explicit Start reaches readiness.
Use anchored command menus, local popovers and persistent inspectors with consistent actions, keyboard focus and immediate modal opening and closing.
Resize and restore Service/Chat panels across wide and narrow layouts without replacing the Service iframe or losing composer context.
Render safe Markdown in assistant messages, including tables and code, while escaping HTML and blocking unsafe links and automatic Markdown image requests.
Keep confirmed content during refresh, use local first-read placeholders, and show real errors and explicit recovery without covering usable Service content.

sections.title: Improvements and fixes
items: Coordinate Stop and send across Chat Sessions and Services, with original submission-key recovery and request/reply readback.
Expose Work name conflicts on the Name field and report imported source names separately from confirmed destination names.
Start managed Work shutdown before blocked control requests or coordination workers exhaust the process budget; retain durable Work and Service choices for restart.

sections.title: Improvements and fixes
items: View Service Agent requests, their Runs and replies; cancel or retry explicitly while imported history stays read-only.
Keep Chat failures visible beside background activity and retain original execution errors through expired-cursor history recovery.
Discard stale local authorization and CSRF failures when a newer authentication flow owns the session, without replaying rejected actions.
Preserve later configuration edits, the original inspected package and explicit naming choices during pending Save or import recovery.

sections.title: Improvements
items: Accept image messages from Desktop Chat and preserve images in private conversation history.
Expose the running Core version and its embedded release notes.
Prepare the default Work environment before readiness and reuse successful image and package-environment checks.
Bundle piwork-brain 1.2.2 with independent application awareness and conditional NiceGUI guidance.
Scope default template CSS and preserve drafts while reporting and recovering from business query failures.

sections.title: Improvements
items: Paste, drop or choose PNG, JPEG and WebP images in Chat.
Keep Create Work buttons stable while submitting or waiting.
View Desktop and Core versions and release notes in About Piwork.
